tagline: An old trade trail turned military road, through Nicolet hemlocks.
intro: From Highway 70 east of Eagle River, Heritage Drive runs south on Military Road and east on Butternut Lake Road, fifteen miles in all through the Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest, a mix of hardwoods, giant hemlocks and pines.

Military Road began as the Old Superior Trail of the Ojibwa, Menominee and Winnebago. In 1863, fearing the British might join the Confederacy, Congress paid to improve it as a supply road from Fort Howard on Green Bay to Fort Wilkins in Michigan. The war itself held up the work until 1869.

moments.title: Franklin Lake
moments.text: On Butternut Lake Road, Civilian Conservation Corps stone and log buildings stand among tall pines and hemlocks, enough to put the campground on the National Register, beside an 892-acre lake with a sandy beach.

moments.title: Franklin Nature Trail
moments.text: The trail passes trees over 400 years old, stops to look at Butternut Lake from under huge hemlocks, and crosses a bog on a boardwalk.
